uncited: *   **Input:** A brick cache with $N$ entries, a multi-channel page-table hierarchy, and a current timestamp $t$ (e.g., frame number).
**Global Brick-Usage Buffer:** An array of size $N$ (number of cache entries).
**LRU Buffer:** An array of size $N$ storing linear indices into the brick cache.
**Global Request Buffer:** A 3D buffer (or equivalent mapping) with one entry per page/brick in the dataset.
Use mask $M$ to rearrange the previous LRU buffer.
Entries where $M[i] == 1$ are moved to the front of the new LRU buffer, preserving their relative order from the previous buffer.
*   **Max Bricks per Timestamp:** A limit on the number of requested bricks per timestamp to control traffic between client and server.
*   **Time Complexity:** LRU update requires scanning the usage buffer and rearranging the LRU buffer ($O(N)$).
Miss compilation requires stream compaction on the request buffer ($O(P)$ where $P$ is number of pages).
